title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

errors: Sign subtlety, not an outright error. With the given formulas, ρ'' := σρ'σ acts by e' ↦ e' + e''. Since σ (the swap) reverses orientation, this ρ'' is the twist along e'' of opposite handedness to ρ'. With e'·e'' = 1 the formula T_a(b) = b + (a·b)a gives T_{e''}(e') = e' − e''. So ρ' and ρ'' as defined are not both positive Dehn twists, and the braid relation ρ'ρ''ρ' = ρ''ρ'ρ'' would hold for ρ' and ρ''^{-1} instead. The note 'anticommutatif' and the circled minus may be precisely Grothendieck's acknowledgement of this sign. The page itself does not resolve it.
The definition of ρ'' is not written explicitly (only ρ' is given on e', e''). It is recovered from σρ'σ = ρ''.

ideas.what: Gluing two cylinders along both pairs of ends to get a torus, with compatibility of orientation torsors ω(X') ≅ ω(X''), and an antisymmetric pairing to ω(X'∧X'')
ideas.modern_name: Pants/cylinder decomposition gluing data with orientation torsors; antisymmetry of the intersection form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates; intersection form). The Lego formalism is Grothendieck's (Esquisse), later developed by Hatcher–Thurston, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3, Teichmüller tower / Lego in general terms; not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Orientation-reversing involutions σ', σ'' conjugate Dehn twists to their inverses; the swap σ exchanges the twists ρ' and ρ''
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group of the torus ≅ GL(2,Z); reflection/twist presentation of PGL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke; standard mapping class group theory)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse mentions the role of the extended Teichmüller groups and of complex conjugation, but not these explicit relations

ideas.what: Dehn twist acting on H_1 as a transvection: ρ'(e'') = e' + e''
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 (Picard–Lefschetz formula), in a different context

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch computation of the extended (1,1) modular group, GL(2,Z) generated by reflections and Dehn twists, inside the Teichmüller-tower program. It is mathematically standard. The only mildly interesting point is the explicit attention to orientation torsors and to the sign/anticommutativity when gluing, which is consistent with the Esquisse's insistence on including orientation reversal.
transcription_corrections: 'σ', σ'' un dépendent [?] pas du "cocycle [?] d'orientation"' should most likely read 'σ', σ'' ne dépendent pas du "choix d'orientations"'. The handwriting suggests 'ne' and 'choix'/'couple', not 'cocycle'.
'e' e'' fixent les 2 orientations' reads better as 'e' e'' fixent les orientations, et aussi une 2-orientation sur X', X'' (?)', followed by struck-through words and then 'X', X'', d'où ρ', ρ''.
The circled '(−)' and the arrow '↘ ω(X'∧X'')' belong to the 'anticommutatif' remark: the pairing ω(X')⊗ω(X'')→ω(X'∧X'') is anticommutative.
'σ'' e'' = e''' appears as '= +e''' with a correction mark.
The bottom-left formulas 'ρ'(e') = e'' and 'ρ'(e'') = e' + e''' are written in the margin, not after the relations block.
